doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Worry over New York clubs surviving
summary: Concern about Small's, Mezzrow, Fat Cat and the larger clubs surviving the shutdown and rents.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. We’re hoping that those venues and festivals can still exist in 2021.

I know, Monk, that’s such a great point, and you know recently, well last week reading things about great iconic clubs in New York like Small’s that are really — major performance clubs, of course the Blue Note, the Vanguard, Dizzy’s, and Jazz Standard and those places, I’m assuming have enough, are financially secure to survive this. But other iconic clubs that are really like the heart and soul that give so many artists an opportunity like Small’s and Mezzro and Fat Cat and they’re like you said, I don’t know if the New York landlords are being nice and letting them get a break on their rent. I don’t know. I hope so. I don’t know what’s going to happen.
